page: Microsoft Azure DC8ads_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core to deliver 8 dedicated vCPUs. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside vector acceleration support including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. Cryptographic acceleration is also enabled via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes an integrated local SSD of 322 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable for external block storage needs. No physical GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording a score of 3022.67, situating the instance in the top 25%. Multi-core performance across stress-ng (12053.56) and Geekbench (6824.0) places it consistently within the middle 50% tier. PassMark testing records a CPU mark of 13997.18, with encryption achieving 8919.32 and database operations reaching 3628.22. Memory performance is verified by an in-memory Redis throughput of 10.12 million SET operations per second, scoring 2252.77 on the PassMark memory suite.

Balancing dedicated AMD compute resources, local high-speed SSD capacity, and balanced memory allocation, the DC8ads_v6 offers efficient resource utilization for common operational footprints. It is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, caching layers, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, backend microservices, and continuous integration pipelines.
